cheap_tests_in_order: 1. Hand-read the un-glossed 1816-era letters against Bourdeau's 162 confirmed values and the Decazes/Florida crib vocabulary already in key.tsv, proposing new values only where a group fits the same word in >=2 independent contexts (rule 4, S grade). No control needed for a crib-driven hand read (the brief's own framing); report a shuffled-order coverage control per rule 3 regardless.

cheap_test_done.method: Concordance of every un-keyed group in the 16 un-glossed 1816-era records, ranked by frequency, read by eye against already-keyed neighbours and the whole corpus (including the 4 glossed records, for cross-checking). Proposed a value only where the same group sits in an identical short frame in >=2 independent letters, or is confirmed a second time against its own glossed value inside the crib letter itself.
cheap_test_done.target: 1816 un-glossed target set (16 records, 7,492 main-code groups, nulls excluded): coverage 3,268/7,492 = 0.4362 before -> 3,406/7,492 = 0.4546 after 3 new S-grade values (+138 tokens, +1.84 points). Whole corpus (25 main-code records, 9,286 groups): 4,342/9,286 = 0.4676 -> 4,505/9,286 = 0.4851.
cheap_test_done.control: Shuffled-order control (3 seeds), same key, same 16 records, group order shuffled within each record: 3,406/7,492 = 0.4546 every seed -- identical to the target's own 'after' figure. This is expected, not a finding: tools/decode_key.py is a pure per-token substitution (no neighbour-dependence), so the coverage fraction cannot depend on group order by construction. Reported per the brief's rule-3 requirement; see NOTES.md for why it is uninformative about reading coherence specifically (a word-sequence language-model control would be needed for that, not run this cap).
cheap_test_done.verdict: Partial gain: 3 new S-grade key values (1378=a, 154=a [homophone of 1378], 605=enza [homophone of the already-glossed 1606]), each attested in >=2 independent un-glossed letters (154 and 1378 both immediately before 'V.E.'; 605 completing 'confer[enza]' after the already-keyed stem 2403=confer, cross-checked against the crib letter R9566's own glossed 1606=enza for the same word). No group among the Decazes/Florida content vocabulary itself (Cuba, Isola, Cattolica, Onis, cessione) recurred enough in the un-glossed set to confirm a new value; those themes are already exhausted in Bourdeau's 162. One unresolved lead (group 2261 + already-keyed 'do', collocating with 'Inghil' twice) named in NOTES.md, not committed. No letter reads through. Per CLAUDE.md rule 5 as amended, this is a control-backed reproducible gain over the inherited key, not a negative and not found-solved: `partial`.
